stories.headline: Anthropic's amended S-1 says future models may 'imminently' meet its AI-accelerated R&D threshold

key_facts.fact: In its amended S-1 (S-1/A) filed with the SEC on Nov 2, 2026, Anthropic added a risk factor saying internal estimates and expectations for future models indicate it 'may imminently meet' its Responsible Scaling Policy's definition of 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI'.
key_facts.excerpt: our internal estimates and our expectations regarding future models, rather than our current models, indicate that we may imminently meet our Responsible Scaling Policy's definition of "dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI."

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says it has not designated any current model as exceeding the threshold and continues to assess the underlying data.
key_facts.excerpt: We have not designated any of our current models as exceeding this threshold, and we continue to assess the underlying data.

key_facts.fact: The filing admits Anthropic has in the past failed to spot a significant acceleration in its rate of development until after it occurred, because its evidence comes largely from lagging indicators.
key_facts.excerpt: "we have in the past not identified, and may in the future not identify, a significant acceleration in our rate of development until after it has occurred."

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says it does not anticipate being able to safely use Claude to fully autonomously design and build successive frontier models without meaningful human supervision, and is considering RSP updates to keep humans in control of frontier model development.
key_facts.excerpt: we are considering updates to our Responsible Scaling Policy to keep humans in control of frontier model development at Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: Under RSP version 3.4 (effective July 8, 2026), the 'dramatic acceleration' route is defined as observing or expecting double the rate of progress in aggregate AI capabilities, measured over at least three model generations and attributable to automated research.
key_facts.excerpt: defined as observing or expecting "double the rate of progress" in aggregate AI capabilities ... measured over at least three model generations

key_facts.fact: Compared with the October S-1, the amendment changes the tense on missed accelerations and adds that Anthropic is weighing requiring human review of certain research decisions.
key_facts.excerpt: It is considering RSP updates to keep humans in control of frontier model development, and to require human review of certain research decisions.

stories.headline: MIT researchers: GPT-6 Astra edited 0.016% of a Qwen model's weights, raising math score 7.9% to 48.1%

key_facts.fact: Researchers including MIT's Omar Khattab published 'Sparks of Weight-Space Programming', arguing LLMs can natively read and write neural network weights without gradient-based training.
key_facts.excerpt: All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops... We call this Weight-Space Programming.

key_facts.fact: Asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math, GPT-6 Astra traced its reasoning loops to one direction written by the MLPs of layers 15 and 19 and subtracted it from 131,072 weights, 0.016% of the model.
key_facts.excerpt: Astra traced the looping to one direction written by the MLPs of layers 15 and 19, and subtracted that direction from 64 output columns in each (131,072 weights)

key_facts.fact: With 50 forward passes, MATH-500 rose from 7.9% to 48.1%, GSM8K from 13.8% to 67.1% and IFEval instruction-following from 21.0% to 62.3%; answers hitting the token limit fell from 93% to 33.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: MATH-500 accuracy 7.9% -> 48.1%; GSM8K 13.8% -> 67.1%; IFEval 21.0% -> 62.3%; MATH-500 responses reaching the token limit 93.0% -> 33.1%

key_facts.fact: Astra worked through a CPU-only Python kernel over the weights, with no gradient descent, no internet and no access to the evaluation benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: We asked a frontier LLM ("Astra") to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math by editing its weights directly, with no gradient descent and no training.

key_facts.fact: An independent re-run of the published edited checkpoint on full MATH-500 scored 51.0%.
key_facts.excerpt: The edited model scored 51.0%, with 31.6% of answers hitting the token limit.

key_facts.fact: The authors say they are now building a benchmark and harness for LLMs to explore and write weights.
key_facts.excerpt: We think neural network weights will soon be natively optimized by LLMs that deliberately reason about the weights. We are now building a benchmark to evaluate, and a harness to help LLMs explore and write weights.

stories.headline: Smugglers move Samsung and SK Hynix HBM into China via a loophole; Huawei's 960DT leans on it

key_facts.fact: Smugglers package export-controlled HBM from Samsung and SK Hynix on boards with cheap low-end server processors, because US export rules assess a package's computing power by the processor, not the memory, according to The Information.
key_facts.excerpt: They are then paired with expensive HBM from Samsung and SK hynix, that, on their own, are banned for export to China. But because export control rules only look at the performance of the server processor and not at the other components attached to it, this allows the HBM chips attached inside them to slip under the radar.

key_facts.fact: In Shenzhen workshops, technicians heat the boards to melt the solder, lift off the memory stacks and discard the processors; the failure rate is high.
key_facts.excerpt: Local technicians apply heat to the board to melt the solder, detach only the necessary HBM, and discard the remaining server processors... the failure rate is high because applying heat too quickly or for an extended period can cause the memory stack to warp or crack.

key_facts.fact: A Chinese broker said one HBM3E unit now sells for about $4,000 in China, up from several hundred dollars a year ago; with 6 to 8 stacks per AI chip, memory alone costs $24,000 to $32,000.
key_facts.excerpt: the price of a single HBM3E, which traded for several hundred dollars just a year ago, has recently soared to about $4,000. A single AI chip package requires 6 to 8 HBMs. The memory price alone amounts to $24,000 to $32,000.

key_facts.fact: Huawei told some customers its next flagship AI chip, the Ascend 960DT, will largely use Samsung and SK Hynix HBM, and advised some customers to source the memory themselves.
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei Technologies, whose next-generation Ascend 960DT AI accelerator is expected to rely heavily on HBM from Samsung Electronics and SK hynix... the company has reportedly asked some AI chip customers to source the memory themselves.

key_facts.fact: The Ascend 960DT is expected in Q1 2027 with double the memory bandwidth and capacity of Huawei's current chip; CXMT's HBM3E yields are reportedly just 20%-30%, versus about 70% at SK Hynix.
key_facts.excerpt: Expected in the first quarter of 2027, the Ascend 960DT is set to double the memory bandwidth and capacity of Huawei's current AI processor... CXMT's HBM3E yields remain at just 20%–30%, well below the approximately 70% achieved by South Korea's SK hynix.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix said it strictly complies with US and Korean export controls and has not supplied Huawei since US restrictions began in 2020.
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix stated, "We are strictly complying with relevant laws and regulations, including the export control regulations of the U.S. and South Korea," adding that it has never supplied products to Huawei since the implementation of U.S. export regulations in 2020.

key_facts.fact: Apple blamed supply constraints for weak iPad sales: iPad revenue fell 10% to $6.2 billion, below the $6.7 billion analysts expected; COO Sabih Khan did not rule out further price increases.
key_facts.excerpt: The company also blamed supply constraints for weak iPad sales in the quarter... iPad revenue was $6.2 billion, below analysts' expectations of $6.7 billion. The figure was also down 10% from the prior year... did not rule out future price increases on Apple devices.

stories.headline: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island in Hormuz on eve of midterms as Brent posts biggest drop since July

key_facts.fact: The US military launched limited strikes on Iranian targets on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, Nov. 2, which US officials described as defensive, after Iran's IRGC fired at an American aircraft.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. military launched limited, defensive strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, three U.S. officials told CBS News. A senior U.S. official said the strikes targeted Iran's Qeshm Island after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired at an American aircraft.

key_facts.fact: Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm and Hengam islands and in mainland Bandar Abbas; unlike earlier in the war, the strikes were not publicly announced, and Trump had previously said the US would not strike Iran before the midterms.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian state media reported explosions being heard on the islands of Qeshm and Hengam in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, and in the nearby mainland area of Bandar Abbas. Unlike earlier in the war, the strikes were not publicly announced. President Donald Trump previously said the U.S. wouldn't launch strikes on Iran before the midterms.

key_facts.fact: The IRGC said it shot down two US MQM-170 drones south of Qeshm and an MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: The IRGC did not comment but said its forces had shot down two US MQM-170 drones south of the island and a US MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: It was the first attack on Qeshm Island since June; the war began on Feb. 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran and closed the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: In the first attack since June on Qeshm Island, which serves as the primary platform for Iran's "asymmetric" naval power... the war, which began on February 28 when the US and Israel launched strikes across Iran, triggering the closure of the critical Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Hours before the strikes, Trump wrote that a deal 'could happen' and that 'Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible'; Iran's chief negotiator Ghalibaf said Tuesday 'the ball is now in America's court to prevent war'.
key_facts.excerpt: On Tuesday, Iran's chief negotiator with the US, parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, stated: "The ball is now in America's court to prevent war."

key_facts.fact: Qatari mediators expect US and Iranian feedback on a new proposal within 36 hours; Qatar said Doha is working 'towards an interim deal'.
key_facts.excerpt: Qatari mediators expect feedback from Iranian and U.S. negotiators on new ideas aimed at getting both sides closer to a deal to end the war within 36 hours... "We remain hopeful that there is still a chance for a deal to take place," he said, adding Doha was working "towards an interim deal".

key_facts.fact: On Monday, Brent crude settled at $104.77, down 7.6%, and WTI fell 7.4% to $96.46, back below $100 — both benchmarks' biggest one-day percentage drops since July 27.
key_facts.excerpt: January Brent crude settled at $104.77 a barrel, down $8.66, or 7.6%, and December WTI crude fell 7.4% to $96.46, back below $100. Both benchmarks had their biggest one-day percentage drops since July 27

key_facts.fact: After reports of the strikes, Brent rose 0.5% to $105.25 in early Asian trade.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures rose 0.5 per cent to $105.25 per barrel while West Texas Intermediate crude was also up 0.5 per cent to $96.93 per barrel.

stories.headline: Russia hits Ukraine's grid with 59 cruise and 17 ballistic missiles as US sets Abu Dhabi talks

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said Russia launched 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles overnight into Tuesday, Nov. 3, hitting power plants and substations from Odesa to Rivne.
key_facts.excerpt: President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Russia had launched 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles, hitting power plants and substations from the Black Sea port of Odesa in the south to Rivne in the west of the country.

key_facts.fact: DTEK, Ukraine's largest private power producer, said three of its five thermal power plants were knocked offline, with outages in Kyiv and at least six other regions.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's largest private energy-generating company DTEK said three of its five thermal power plants had been knocked offline. Ukrainian officials said the damage forced power outages across the capital Kyiv and at least six other regions.

key_facts.fact: A strike on a hospital in Kharkiv injured 73 people and damaged its cardiology department; more than 180,000 people lost power in the Zhytomyr region.
key_facts.excerpt: "the Russians directly struck a city clinical hospital. Seventy-three people were injured, and the cardiology department, where people were receiving treatment, was damaged." ... More than 180,000 people were without power in the Zhytomyr region on Tuesday morning

key_facts.fact: Russia said Ukraine set fire to a major oil refinery in Yaroslavl, and Moscow's mayor said nearly 500 drones heading toward the capital region were destroyed.
key_facts.excerpt: In Russia, Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said nearly 500 drones heading towards the capital region were destroyed.

key_facts.fact: US envoy Steve Witkoff said the US will mediate working-level Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, focused on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian issues; the Kremlin confirmed a delegation led by Vladimir Medinsky.
key_facts.excerpt: "The Russian delegation will arrive on November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi to take part in trilateral talks," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters. The Russian delegation will be led by Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky

key_facts.fact: Witkoff said US negotiators will meet the UK, France, Germany, the EU and NATO in Brussels this week on security guarantees for Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Witkoff also said in his post that US negotiators would meet this week in Brussels with representatives from the UK, France, Germany, the EU and Nato to discuss "security guarantees for Ukraine, Europe's postwar security architecture and economic opportunities to support Ukraine's reconstruction".

key_facts.fact: A Russian strike on a school used as an aid distribution point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia, killed at least 31 people, with almost 50 missing; the strike came after a rare Kherson truce ended Sunday.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 31 people were killed when Russian forces bombed a school being used as an aid distribution point in a village near the front line in Ukraine's southeastern region of Zaporizhzhia yesterday... almost 50 people were still missing

stories.headline: Australia's central bank hikes to 4.85%, an 18-year high, in split 6-3 vote

key_facts.fact: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.85% on Nov. 3, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: At its meeting today, the Board decided to increase the cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.85 per cent.

key_facts.fact: The decision was split: six members voted to hike and three to hold at 4.60%.
key_facts.excerpt: six members voted to increase the cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.85 per cent; three members voted to leave the cash rate target unchanged at 4.60 per cent.

key_facts.fact: The RBA cited fuel and commodity prices affected by the Middle East conflict and said AI-related investment is driving rapid growth in prices of technology-related goods; inflation is now not expected to reach the top of the 2-3% target until late 2027, about three quarters later than forecast.
key_facts.excerpt: This partly reflects higher fuel and other commodity prices affected by the conflict in the Middle East... AI-related investment is driving rapid growth in prices for technology-related goods... not expected to reach the top of the 2–3 per cent target range until late 2027, around three quarters later than previously forecast.

key_facts.fact: It is the fifth rate hike of 2026 and the highest cash rate since late 2008.
key_facts.excerpt: It is the highest cash rate since late 2008. It is the fifth time the bank has lifted rates in 2026.

key_facts.fact: The statement dropped language about willingness to hike further; Governor Michele Bullock said 'We're basically preserving our options'. Home values in major cities fell 1.4% in October.
key_facts.excerpt: It omitted a reference that it was willing to hike further if needed, a line that has been included in each statement since June... "We're basically preserving our options." ... Home values in major cities fell 1.4% in October

key_facts.fact: Canstar estimates a borrower with a A$500,000 loan could pay about A$77 more a month.
key_facts.excerpt: Canstar estimates a borrower with a $500,000 loan could pay about $77 more a month, while someone with a $1 million loan could face an extra $153 a month in repayments.

stories.headline: UK's NCSC: China, Russia will routinely use AI cyberattacks for geopolitical goals by 2028

key_facts.fact: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre, part of GCHQ, published its 2026 Annual Review, 'The State of the Cyber Nation', on Nov. 3.
key_facts.excerpt: NCSC CEO Richard Horne launches the Annual Review 2026: The State of the Cyber Nation.

key_facts.fact: The NCSC judges it 'highly likely' that by 2028 China, Russia and other nation states will routinely use AI cyber capabilities to achieve geopolitical goals, and that AI-powered malware will have been used in a ransomware attack on UK critical national infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: By 2028, it is highly likely China, Russia, and other nation states will routinely use AI cyber to achieve their geopolitical goals... It is also highly likely that between now and 2028, AI-powered malware will have been used in a ransomware attack on UK CNI.

key_facts.fact: It calls China the 'most sophisticated and sustained cyber challenge' facing the UK and Russia currently the 'most audacious' cyber threat.
key_facts.excerpt: China's adversarial cyber activity represents the most sophisticated and sustained cyber challenge facing the UK... Russia currently represents the most audacious cyber threat to the UK.

key_facts.fact: The agency says it is almost certain AI will act as a force multiplier for skilled attackers, accelerating reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery and exploit development.
key_facts.excerpt: It is almost certain AI will act as a force multiplier across the cyber threat landscape... enhancing multiple stages of the attack lifecycle, including reconnaissance, social engineering, vulnerability discovery, and coding for exploit development.

key_facts.fact: CEO Richard Horne wrote that UK cyber resilience 'is not yet where it should be' and the threat 'has increased faster than our defensive capabilities'.
key_facts.excerpt: The UK's cyber resilience is not yet where it should be. The cyber threat has increased faster than our defensive capabilities, leaving too many organisations vulnerable

key_facts.fact: Horne said Iran is still carrying out malicious cyber operations globally, including against the UK, despite the Middle East conflict, and announced a new National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability Centre that will use AI to find vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Despite the pressures of the Middle East conflict, Iran is still carrying out malicious cyber operations globally including against the UK... a new National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability Centre will use AI to identify vulnerabilities across our critical infrastructure and economy.

stories.headline: SUSE to cut about 10% of its 1,900 staff, saying AI is 'fundamentally shifting' software work

key_facts.fact: In a Monday memo seen by The Register, SUSE CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen announced a reduction of approximately 10% of the open source company's 1,900-strong global workforce.
key_facts.excerpt: In an email to the 1,900 strong workforce on Monday - seen by The Register - CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen... "We are announcing a reduction of SUSE's global workforce of approximately 10 percent,"

key_facts.fact: Van Leeuwen wrote that 'automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate' and that 'the requirement for some existing roles has greatly diminished'.
key_facts.excerpt: "What is clear is that automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate. AI capabilities are advancing exponentially, forcing us to radically reimagine our work... The requirement for some existing roles has greatly diminished."

key_facts.fact: Affected staff will be informed by Nov. 4; the rest of the company will see the fiscal 2027 strategy on Nov. 16.
key_facts.excerpt: Staff caught up in the redundancies will be informed by November 4... The rest of the organization will get a look at the fiscal year 2027 strategy on November 16.

key_facts.fact: SUSE is owned by Swedish private equity firm EQT, which bought it for $2.5 billion in 2018 and took it private again in 2023; in September SUSE had offered staff voluntary separation.
key_facts.excerpt: Back in September, we reported that the company was asking old hands if they would take "voluntary separation."... Back in 2018, EQT bought SUSE from Microfocus for $2.5 billion... later in 2023, EQT chose to take the company private again.

stories.headline: Brazil's largest crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin halts withdrawals after $46M breach

key_facts.fact: Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest cryptocurrency exchange, confirmed on Monday, Nov. 2, a security incident involving about $46.3 million in assets, according to Arkham data.
key_facts.excerpt: Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest cryptocurrency exchange, confirmed Monday that it suffered a security incident involving approximately $46.3 million in assets, according to Arkham data.

key_facts.fact: The exchange said it 'identified and swiftly contained' the incident early that morning, suspended deposits and withdrawals, and said customers were not affected and no data was breached.
key_facts.excerpt: "We identified and swiftly contained a security incident in one of our systems early this morning," the exchange said in a post on X. Mercado Bitcoin temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals... the incident did not affect customers or result in a data breach.

key_facts.fact: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the stablecoin issuer froze more than 4.5 million USDT linked to the incident.
key_facts.excerpt: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino confirmed that the stablecoin issuer had frozen more than 4.5 million USDT linked to the incident.

key_facts.fact: An Arkham analyst said the attacker was sweeping funds from older deposit addresses and selling memecoins and altcoins.
key_facts.excerpt: Arkham analyst Emmett Gallic said the attacker was sweeping funds from older deposit addresses and selling memecoins and other altcoins.

key_facts.fact: The breach follows Thursday's $6 billion Binance hack and a string of other exploits, including a $2.65 million Polymarket exploit.
key_facts.excerpt: Mercado Bitcoin's incident comes amid a string of security breaches and exploits across the crypto industry in recent days, following Thursday's $6 billion hack of Binance. That same day, Polymarket was hit by a $2.65 million exploit

stories.headline: Nasdaq falls 1.1% as investors keep rotating out of tech; Dow rises and gold gains 1.8%

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 2 the Nasdaq fell 1.07% to 25,164.32 and the S&P 500 lost 0.51% to 7,541.40 after giving up early gains, while the Dow rose 0.41% to 51,983.98.
key_facts.excerpt: The tech-heavy Nasdaq dipped 1.07% to end at 25,164.32, while the S&P 500 shed 0.51% to close at 7,541.40. Both benchmarks were up as much as 1.4% and 1.1%, respectively. The Dow Jones Industrial Average outperformed, rising 213.67 points, or 0.41%, to 51,983.98.

key_facts.fact: Oracle fell 8% after saying it plans to sell $10 billion in common stock and $10 billion in bonds to finance its AI buildout.
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle shares also declined 8% after the company said it plans to sell $10 billion in common stock as well as $10 billion in bonds to finance its AI buildout.

key_facts.fact: Old-economy stocks drove the Dow: Sherwin-Williams rose almost 6% and Home Depot 3.6%, with Honeywell, 3M and Boeing up more than 2%.
key_facts.excerpt: Gains in so-called old economy stocks such as Sherwin-Williams and Home Depot powered the Dow, rising almost 6% and 3.6%, respectively. Honeywell International, 3M and Boeing were also up more than 2% each.

key_facts.fact: Most S&P 500 stocks still rose, helped by the 7.6% drop in Brent crude to $104.77.
key_facts.excerpt: The mixed performance for indexes came even though the majority of stocks within the S&P 500 climbed. They benefited from a 7.6% drop for the price of a barrel of Brent crude to $104.77.

key_facts.fact: Gold rose 1.81% to $3,969.60 and the 10-year Treasury yield fell about 3 basis points to 4.91%.
